qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Cecilia Strada (S&D), Udo Bullmann (S&D), Marit Maij (S&D), Marta Temido (S&D), Murielle Laurent (S&D), Leoluca Orlando (Verts/ALE), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Marc Botenga (The Left), Benedetta Scuderi (Verts/ALE), Ilaria Salis (The Left), Catarina Vieira (Verts/ALE), Sebastian Tynkkynen (ECR), Charles Goerens (Renew), Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE), Irene Tinagli (S&D), Hilde Vautmans (Renew), Irena Joveva (Renew), Marco Tarquinio (S&D), Barry Andrews (Renew) Subject:

In its resolutions of 27 November 20251 and 9 July 20262 on Sudan, Parliament condemned external interference fuelling the war, including arms transfers, mercenary deployment, gold smuggling and illicit financial networks. The EU has repeatedly called for an end to all external support to the warring parties, and in July 2026 adopted restrictive measures targeting the Sudanese gold trade. Against this backdrop: 1.

Is the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy (VP/HR) considering designating illicit gold trafficking networks operating through the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and neighbouring countries, as the UK has already done?

Will the VP/HR and the Commission commit to assessing whether the UAE should be added to the EU and Financial Action Task Force lists of high-risk third countries with strategic deficiencies in anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing, given its well-documented role in enabling the illicit gold trade that is sustaining this conflict?

Is the VP/HR ready to raise the UAE’s involvement in the illicit gold trade and its role in sustaining the conflict in Sudan at the next summit between the EU and the Gulf Cooperation Council (originally scheduled for 24 October 2026), as well as at other bilateral and multilateral meetings involving the UAE, and to seek concrete commitments on accountability?

European Parliament resolution of 27 November 2025 on the escalation of the war and the humanitarian catastrophe in Sudan (OJ C, C/2026/1717, 24.4.2026, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/C/2026/1717/oj). 2 European Parliament resolution of 9 July 2026 on the threat of war crimes, the escalating violations of international humanitarian law and the human rights situation in El-Obeid, Sudan (texts adopted, P10_TA(2026)0267). 1
